description:
**Divergence**: TasksBackend::update_task_per_user (crate-jmap-tasks-server/src/backend.rs:236) provides a default impl that delegates to update_object, which silently bumps the shared `updated` timestamp. draft-tasks-06 §4.5.1 MANDATES that a patch limited to per-user properties MUST NOT touch the shared `updated` timestamp.

**Caller-observable effect**: a multi-user backend that ships TasksBackend with this default in place will, on any per-user-only patch by user A, invalidate the shared Task/changes state for users B/C/D. The rustdoc only says "SHOULD override" — a SHOULD against a spec-stated MUST. Single-user deployments are unaffected; this only burns in multi-user.

**Sibling positions**:
- jmap-mail-server (canonical extension-server): every spec-mandated mutation is REQUIRED (no default). `blob_exists` doc-comment at crate-jmap-mail-server/src/backend.rs:194-198 is the explicit workspace policy statement on why spec-mandated methods get no default.
- jmap-chat-server: all spec-mandated mutations (apply_space_patch, apply_space_metadata_patch, generate_invite_code) are REQUIRED; defaults exist ONLY for deployment-policy hooks (slow-mode, custom-emoji authorization, contact-block lookups).
- jmap-calendars-server: SAME ANTI-PATTERN as tasks (see bd:JMAP-ic0j.26).
- jmap-metadata-server: partial-compliance default (filter args silently dropped, handler post-filters created/updated but not destroyed) — see sibling bead being filed.

**Recommendation**: drop the default; require backends to provide an impl, exactly like mail-server's pattern for `import_email` / `parse_email` / etc. The kit cannot uphold the §4.5.1 invariant on the backend's behalf without storage-layer access.

**Cross-references**: bd:JMAP-ic0j.26 (calendars-server analogue, OPEN). This bead is the tasks-server instance of the same workspace anti-pattern.
title: tasks-server: TasksBackend::update_task_per_user default silently violates draft-tasks-06 §4.5.1 in multi-user deployments
